spatial_claims.claim: Points A, C, D, B are collinear on line AB with ordering A-C-D-B
C is the midpoint of AB, so AC = CB
D lies between C and B
AD = AC + CD, requiring C between A and D
CB is cut at D, requiring D between C and B
CB is cut at D into segments CD and DB, requiring C-D-B ordering

configuration_map: All points lie on a single straight line AB with fixed ordering A-C-D-B. C is the midpoint of AB (AC = CB). D is strictly between C and B. Segments: AC = CB, AD = AC + CD = CB + CD, CB = CD + DB. The entire proof operates on this collinear arrangement, applying rectangle and square area identities (Props 2.1, 2.3, 2.4) to various sub-segments. No auxiliary points off the line are constructed; no angles, triangles, or circles are involved.
pass_reason: The proof is purely algebraic, manipulating rectangle and square area identities on a collinear arrangement of four points A-C-D-B. The only spatial content is the betweenness relations on a single line, which are trivially consistent throughout all steps. Every application of Propositions 2.1, 2.3, and 2.4 correctly references the appropriate segments given the established A-C-D-B ordering. No angle decompositions, interior/exterior claims, or non-trivial spatial configurations are present.
